1	Test Requirements
2	Technical Assessment - Rent Collection
3	
4	Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router) - TypeScript - Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Storage) - Prisma - shadcn/ui - Tailwind CSS
5	
6	Time: the timer above is what counts, normally 4 hours (about 30 min reading - 3 h building - 30 min write-ups and submission)
7	
8	Read This First
9	
10	AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot...) are allowed and expected. We assess whether you understand and control what gets built. Code you cannot explain counts as not done.
11	
12	Hidden tests. We run automated tests against every rule in this brief, including edge cases that are not in the examples:
13	your billing functions, about 50 hidden cases, run under TZ=UTC, TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur and TZ=America/New_York
14	your HTTP API, called as each seeded account, including requests about other organizations' records and concurrent requests
15	your Supabase Data API and Storage bucket, called directly with your publishable key and each user's token
16	your payment webhook, with valid, forged, duplicated, concurrent and out-of-order callbacks
17	AI logs. Export the transcript of every AI session you use (in Claude Code: /export) into an ai-logs/ folder in your repo. We do not count how much you used AI. We look at how you directed it, what you checked and what you corrected.
18	Walkthrough. If your submission passes, the interview starts with a 30-minute walkthrough of your code: we pick parts of it, ask "what happens if...", and ask you to make a small change live.
19	Priorities. A correct and secure subset beats a complete but sloppy app. If time runs short, work in this order: billing functions (section 3), access control (6), payments (4), webhook (5), UI (9). Say in your README what you skipped.
20	Names are a contract. Table names, column names, endpoint paths, file paths and response shapes in this brief are what our tests use. You may add more of your own.
21	1. The Business
22	
23	You are building part of the rent collection module of a property management platform used by Malaysian property management companies.
24	
25	Each organization (a property management company) rents units to tenants under leases.
26	A lease produces invoices: an optional deposit, plus one rent invoice per monthly period.
27	Tenants pay by cash, by bank transfer (with an uploaded slip), or online through a payment gateway. Payments are allocated to invoices.
28	Business timezone: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no daylight saving). Currency: MYR (RM). 1 ringgit = 100 sen.
29	Your server runs in UTC and our assessors work from several timezones. Every date and time the app shows or accepts is Malaysia time, whatever the timezone of the server or of the viewer's device.
30	Roles
31	ROLE WHO CAN
32	manager Organization admin Everything in their organization: create leases, record payments (approved immediately), approve, reject and void payments, read the audit log
33	staff Front desk Read their organization's leases, invoices and payments; record payments (these wait for a manager's approval)
34	tenant Renter Read their own profile, leases, invoices and payments; update their own phone number; pay online
35	
36	A staff member or manager belongs to exactly one organization. Nobody ever sees another organization's data.
37	
38	2. Local Setup and Seed Data
39	
40	Develop against a local Supabase stack (Docker and the Supabase CLI), not a cloud project. See Supabase local development. We grade by running your project on our machine from a fresh clone, with exactly these commands:
41	
42	npx supabase start # starts the stack from your supabase/config.toml
43	npx supabase db reset # rebuilds the database from supabase/migrations/
44	npm install
45	cp .env.example .env.local # we replace keys with the values from `npx supabase status` if they differ
46	npm run seed
47	npm run build && npm start
48	Commit supabase/config.toml, supabase/migrations/, and an .env.example that lists every variable your app needs, with local values and a comment saying where each one comes from.
49	npm run seed creates exactly the data below on a freshly reset database, through your normal code paths (your lease creation and payment logic), so the invoices and allocations it produces are the ones your app would produce.
50	All seeded accounts share one password of your choice, which you submit with your work.
51	Organizations and accounts
52	ORGANIZATION ACCOUNT ROLE NOTES
53	Northwind Properties manager@northwind.test manager
54	Northwind Properties staff@northwind.test staff
55	Northwind Properties aisyah@northwind.test tenant Tenant "Aisyah Rahman"
56	Northwind Properties ben@northwind.test tenant Tenant "Ben Lim"
57	Northwind Properties probe@northwind.test tenant Tenant "Probe Tenant" (our tests create payments and leases for this tenant)
58	Beta Realty manager@beta.test manager
59	Beta Realty chen@beta.test tenant Tenant "Chen Wei"
60	Units and leases
61	ORGANIZATION UNIT TENANT START END MONTHLY RENT DEPOSIT
62	Northwind A-12-3 Aisyah Rahman 2026-01-31 2026-07-15 RM 1,500.00 RM 3,000.00
63	Northwind B-05-1 Ben Lim 2026-01-01 2026-04-15 RM 1,000.29 none
64	Northwind C-01-7 Probe Tenant 2026-02-28 2027-02-27 RM 2,000.00 RM 4,000.00
65	Northwind D-03-2 (no lease)
66	Beta KL-1 Chen Wei 2026-03-15 2027-03-14 RM 2,200.00 RM 4,400.00
67	Payments on Aisyah's lease
68	Cash, RM 3,000.00, received 2026-01-31 10:00 Malaysia time, recorded by the manager.
69	Bank transfer, RM 2,000.00, received 2026-03-01 00:30 Malaysia time, recorded by staff with a slip file, then approved by the manager.
70	3. Billing Rules - lib/billing.ts
71	
72	Create lib/billing.ts (or src/lib/billing.ts). It must be pure: no I/O, no imports from Next.js, React, Supabase or Prisma, and no dependence on the timezone of the machine it runs on. Your app must use it, and we test it directly.
73	
74	export type InvoiceKind = 'deposit' | 'rent'
75	
76	export interface ScheduledInvoice {
77	kind: InvoiceKind
78	periodIndex: number | null // 0, 1, 2... for rent; null for the deposit
79	periodStart: string | null // 'YYYY-MM-DD'; null for the deposit
80	periodEnd: string | null // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive; null for the deposit
81	dueDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
82	amountSen: number // integer
83	}
84	
85	export function generateSchedule(lease: {
86	startDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
87	endDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive (the tenant's last day)
88	monthlyRentSen: number
89	depositSen: number
90	}): ScheduledInvoice[]
91	
92	export type InvoiceStatus = 'paid' | 'partially_paid' | 'unpaid' | 'overdue'
93	
94	export function invoiceStatus(
95	invoice: { dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number },
96	now: Date,
97	): InvoiceStatus
98	
99	export function parseRinggitToSen(input: string): number
100	generateSchedule
101	Validation. Throw an Error if a date is not a real calendar date written as YYYY-MM-DD, if endDate is before startDate, if monthlyRentSen is not a positive integer, or if depositSen is not a non-negative integer.
102	Deposit. If depositSen > 0, the first invoice is the deposit: kind: 'deposit', due on startDate, period fields null.
103	Anchors. Rent periods are anchored on the start date. The anchor of period k is the start date plus k calendar months, always counted from the start date (never from the previous anchor). If that month has fewer days than the start day, use the month's last day. A lease starting on Jan 31 has anchors Jan 31, Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31, Apr 30, and so on.
104	Periods. Period k runs from anchor k to the day before anchor k+1, and is due on anchor k. There is a period for every anchor on or before endDate.
105	Last period. It is cut at endDate. If it is shorter than its full length, it costs monthlyRentSen x days used / days in the full period, rounded half up to the nearest sen. Every other period costs monthlyRentSen.
106	Order. The deposit first, then rent by period index.
107	
108	Worked example (Aisyah's lease):
109	
110	PERIOD KIND DATES DUE AMOUNT
111	deposit 2026-01-31 RM 3,000.00
112	0 rent 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-27 2026-01-31 RM 1,500.00
113	1 rent 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-30 2026-02-28 RM 1,500.00
114	2 rent 2026-03-31 to 2026-04-29 2026-03-31 RM 1,500.00
115	3 rent 2026-04-30 to 2026-05-30 2026-04-30 RM 1,500.00
116	4 rent 2026-05-31 to 2026-06-29 2026-05-31 RM 1,500.00
117	5 rent 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-15 2026-06-30 RM 774.19
118	
119	Period 5 uses 16 of the 31 days from 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-30: 150000 x 16 / 31 = 77419.35, so 77419 sen.
120	
121	invoiceStatus
122	
123	Apply these rules in order:
124	
125	paid if paidSen >= amountSen.
126	overdue if today's Malaysia date is after dueDate. An invoice due 2026-03-01 becomes overdue at 2026-03-02 00:00 Malaysia time (2026-03-01T16:00:00Z), not a moment earlier.
127	partially_paid if paidSen > 0.
128	Otherwise unpaid.
129	parseRinggitToSen
130	
131	Turns what a user types into sen. It accepts digits with optional comma thousands separators (groups of exactly three digits) and an optional decimal part of one or two digits, ignoring whitespace around the value: "1,500.50" gives 150050, "1.15" gives 115, "7" gives 700. Anything else throws an Error, for example "", "-5", "1.234", "1e3", "RM 10", "1,23".
132	
133	4. Payments
134	Recording a payment
135	Staff and managers record cash or bank transfer payments on a lease: the amount, the method, and the date and time the money was received (entered and shown in Malaysia time).
136	A bank transfer needs a slip: a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB, stored in Supabase Storage (section 6). If recording fails after the upload, the file must not be left behind.
137	A payment recorded by a manager is approved immediately. A payment recorded by staff is pending_verification until a manager approves or rejects it.
138	Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.
139	Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)
140	Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
141	Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
142	Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.
143	Payments are never deleted. Every approval, rejection, void and lease creation writes a row to audit_log (who, what, when, details).
144	Allocation
145	
146	When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.
147	
148	The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.
149	
150	All of this must stay correct when requests arrive at the same time. For example, two staff members recording payments on the same lease at once must not exceed the cap together, and a payment approved twice at once is allocated once.
151	
152	Collections report
153	
154	The total of approved payments for each calendar month of received_at in Malaysia time, over a range of months, including months with nothing collected. With the seed data, Northwind's report for 2026-01 to 2026-03 is [{ month: '2026-01', collectedSen: 300000 }, { month: '2026-02', collectedSen: 0 }, { month: '2026-03', collectedSen: 200000 }].
155	
156	5. Online Payments
157	
158	A tenant pays online like this:
159	
160	The tenant clicks Pay now on their lease. Your API creates a gateway bill for the amount due now: the unpaid amounts of the lease's invoices due on or before today's Malaysia date. If nothing is due, refuse. Bill ids must be impossible to guess.
161	In production the tenant would now be redirected to the gateway. In this test, show the bill id and amount: we play the gateway using the simulator below.
162	The gateway calls your webhook, POST /api/webhooks/gateway. Only the webhook can settle a bill. The gateway also sends the tenant back to /payments/return?bill_id=...&paid=true. That page only shows the bill's real status from your database and changes nothing.
163	Webhook
164	
165	The request body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with these fields. The gateway may add more fields in future.
166	
167	FIELD EXAMPLE NOTES
168	id bill_8f3a2c Your bill id (this short example is guessable; yours must not be)
169	paid true true or false
170	paid_amount 210050 Amount in sen; 0 when not paid
171	paid_at 2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800 When it was paid
172	transaction_id TX-000123 Gateway transaction id
173	transaction_status completed completed, failed or pending
174	x_signature 06994f... See below
175	
176	Signature. Take every field in the request except x_signature, sort them by key (ascending by character code), write each one as the key immediately followed by the value, join them with |, and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the resulting string with your secret key GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY, as lowercase hex. Test vector, with the key test_x_signature_key and the six example values above:
177	
178	source: idbill_8f3a2c|paidtrue|paid_amount210050|paid_at2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800|transaction_idTX-000123|transaction_statuscompleted
179	signature: 06994fab2d674e7829144eaa2204631716d3c099b503d38945e92b6296531641
180	
181	Required behavior:
182	
183	SITUATION RESPONSE EFFECT
184	Signature missing or wrong 401 None
185	Unknown bill id 404 None
186	paid=true and paid_amount is not the bill's amount 422 None
187	paid=true, bill pending or failed 200 Bill becomes paid, and one approved online payment is created with received_at = paid_at, then allocated
188	paid=true, bill already paid (a repeat delivery) 200 None
189	paid=false, bill pending 200 Bill becomes failed
190	paid=false, bill already failed (a repeat delivery) 200 None
191	paid=false, bill already paid (late or out of order) 200 None: a paid bill never goes back
192	
193	The gateway retries, so it may deliver the same callback several times, including at the same moment. A bill creates at most one payment, ever. Never log the secret key or whole callback payloads.
194	
195	Simulator
196	
197	Save this as gateway-sim.mjs and run node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false] with GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY set.
198	
199	import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'
200	
201	const [billId, amountSen, paid = 'true'] = process.argv.slice(2)
202	const url = process.env.WEBHOOK_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway'
203	const key = process.env.GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY
204	
205	const myt = new Date(Date.now() + 8 * 3600 * 1000).toISOString()
206	const fields = {
207	id: billId,
208	paid,
209	paid_amount: paid === 'true' ? amountSen : '0',
210	paid_at: `${myt.slice(0, 10)} ${myt.slice(11, 19)} +0800`,
211	transaction_id: `TX-${Date.now()}`,
212	transaction_status: paid === 'true' ? 'completed' : 'failed',
213	}
214	const source = Object.keys(fields).sort().map(k => `${k}${fields[k]}`).join('|')
215	fields.x_signature = createHmac('sha256', key).update(source).digest('hex')
216	
217	const res = await fetch(url, {
218	method: 'POST',
219	headers: { 'content-type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
220	body: new URLSearchParams(fields),
221	})
222	console.log(res.status, await res.text())
223	6. Access Control
224	
225	Access is enforced in two places, and we test both:
226	
227	Your server code: route handlers, Server Actions and server components. Every endpoint must authenticate the caller and check their organization and role itself. A protected page or a hidden button is not a check.
228	The Supabase Data API and Storage, which anyone holding your publishable key can call directly with their own access token.
229	Server code
230	Roles come from your memberships table, and from tenants.user_id for tenants. Never take a role or an organization from anything the user can edit, such as user_metadata.
231	On the server, authenticate with supabase.auth.getUser() or getClaims(), not getSession().
232	A request about a record in another organization, or another tenant's record, gets 404: do not reveal that it exists. A request about a record the caller can see, for an action their role does not allow, gets 403. A request without a valid login gets 401.
233	IDs in request bodies are untrusted too. For example, a manager must not be able to create a lease on another organization's unit or tenant.
234	Our tests call your API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, where the token is a Supabase access token for one of the seeded users. Accept that header as well as the normal session cookie.
235	The service role (secret) key must never reach the browser.
236	Data API
237	
238	This table is the most access allowed through the Supabase Data API, which is PostgREST called with a user's token. Granting less is fine where your app does not need it, with one exception: the tenant portal reads the tenant's own data, and updates their phone number, directly from the browser with supabase-js.
239	
240	TABLE ANON TENANT STAFF MANAGER
241	organizations none read own organization read own organization read own organization
242	memberships none none read own organization read own organization
243	units none read the units of own leases read own organization read own organization
244	tenants none read own row, update only phone read own organization read own organization
245	leases, invoices, payments, payment_allocations, gateway_bills none read the rows of own leases read own organization read own organization
246	audit_log none none none read own organization
247	
248	Every other insert, update or delete through the Data API must fail for everyone. This covers every table, view and function (/rest/v1/rpc/...) you create, not just the ones above. audit_log is append-only for every role, including the service role and the database owner.
249	
250	Storage
251	
252	Bank transfer slips go in a private bucket named payment-slips, under <org_id>/.... Only staff and managers of that organization can upload there, and they read slips through short-lived signed URLs. Tenants, other organizations and anonymous users cannot read, list or upload slips. A payment's slip_path must point to an existing file in its own organization's folder.
253	
254	7. HTTP API
255	
256	Request and response bodies are JSON, except for the webhook. Amounts are integers in sen. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and instants are ISO 8601 with an offset. Errors return { "error": "message" }.
257	
258	METHOD AND PATH WHO SUCCESS OTHER RESPONSES
259	POST /api/leases manager 201 { id } 400 invalid input, 409 overlaps another lease on the unit
260	GET /api/leases/:leaseId staff, manager, the lease's tenant 200, shape below
261	POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments staff, manager 201 { id, status } 400 invalid input, 422 over the cap
262	POST /api/payments/:paymentId/approve manager 200 { status } 409 not pending, 422 over the remaining balance
263	POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject manager 200 { status } 400 missing reason, 409 not pending
264	POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void manager 200 { status } 400 missing reason, 409 not approved
265	POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills the lease's tenant 201 { billId, amountSen } 422 nothing due
266	GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM staff, manager 200 [{ month: 'YYYY-MM', collectedSen }], one entry per month in order 400 invalid range
267	POST /api/webhooks/gateway the gateway see section 5
268	
269	Every endpoint also returns 401, 403 and 404 as described in section 6. Request bodies:
270	
271	// POST /api/leases
272	{ unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
273	
274	// POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments
275	{ amountSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer'; receivedAt: string; slipPath?: string }
276	
277	// POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject and POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void
278	{ reason: string }
279	
280	GET /api/leases/:leaseId returns the invoices in allocation order:
281	
282	{
283	lease: { id: string; unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
284	invoices: {
285	id: string; kind: 'deposit' | 'rent'; periodIndex: number | null; periodStart: string | null; periodEnd: string | null
286	dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number; status: InvoiceStatus
287	}[]
288	payments: {
289	id: string; amountSen: number; unappliedSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer' | 'online'
290	status: 'pending_verification' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'voided'; receivedAt: string
291	}[]
292	}
293	
294	Creating a lease stores the lease and exactly the invoices generateSchedule returns, all or nothing. Leases on the same unit never overlap (both dates are inclusive), even when two requests arrive at the same moment.
295	
296	8. Database
297	Keep every database object in SQL migrations under supabase/migrations/: tables, constraints, RLS policies, grants, functions, triggers, and the storage bucket and its policies. npx supabase db reset must rebuild all of it; nothing may depend on changes made by hand in Supabase Studio. Use Prisma for server-side data access, with prisma/schema.prisma matching the database.
298	Store money as integer sen (bigint), never as a floating-point type. Calendar dates are date, and instants are timestamptz.
299	Required tables and columns (add whatever else you need):
300	TABLE REQUIRED COLUMNS
301	organizations id, name
302	memberships user_id, org_id, role (manager or staff)
303	units id, org_id, name
304	tenants id, org_id, user_id, full_name, email, phone

306	invoices id, org_id, lease_id, kind, period_index, period_start, period_end, due_date, amount_sen
307	payments id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, unapplied_sen, method, status, received_at, slip_path, gateway_bill_id
308	payment_allocations id, org_id, payment_id, invoice_id, amount_sen
309	gateway_bills id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, status (pending, paid or failed)
310	audit_log id, org_id, actor_id, action, entity_id, details, created_at
311	9. UI
312	
313	Use shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS throughout, with toasts for every action (success and error), loading states instead of blank screens, and helpful messages for empty and invalid input. TypeScript in strict mode, without any.
314	
315	Staff and managers:
316	
317	A dashboard with the number of overdue invoices and the collections report for the last 6 months.
318	A list of leases, and a lease page with its invoices (period, due date, amount, paid, status) and payments (with a link to the slip for bank transfers).
319	Recording a payment: the amount typed in ringgit and parsed with parseRinggitToSen, the date and time received in Malaysia time, and a slip upload for bank transfers.

13	export const resolveFetch = (customFetch?: Fetch): Fetch => {
14	  if (customFetch) {

16	  }

18	}

25	 * New-format Supabase API keys (`sb_publishable_…` / `sb_secret_…`) are not JWTs and
26	 * must never be sent as a Bearer token — they belong only in the `apikey` header.
27	 * All other keys (legacy JWT keys, `sb_temp_…` temporary keys, unrecognized `sb_`
28	 * subtypes) keep the Bearer fallback.
29	 */
30	const isNewApiKey = (key: string): boolean =>
31	  key.startsWith('sb_publishable_') || key.startsWith('sb_secret_')
32

34

39	 * Never throws — the server, not the SDK, decides key validity. The key value is never
40	 * included in the message.
41	 */

43	  if (!key.startsWith('sb_') || isNewApiKey(key) || key.startsWith(TEMP_KEY_PREFIX)) {
44	    return
45	  }
46	  const subtype = key.match(/^sb_[a-zA-Z0-9]+_/)?.[0] ?? 'unknown'
47	  if (warnedKeySubtypes.has(subtype)) {
48	    return
49	  }

51	  console.warn(
52	    '@supabase/supabase-js: Unrecognized Supabase API key format. The client will proceed ' +
53	      'and send this key as-is; if you see authentication errors you may need to upgrade ' +
54	      '@supabase/supabase-js to a version that recognizes this key type.'
55	  )
56	}

60	  supabaseUrl: string,
61	  getAccessToken: () => Promise<string | null>,
62	  customFetch?: Fetch,
63	  tracePropagationOptions?: TracePropagationOptions,
64	  options?: { omitApiKeyAsBearer?: boolean }
65	): Fetch => {

70	  // path skips all tracing work with a single truthy check.

11	type Fetch = typeof fetch
12	
13	export const resolveFetch = (customFetch?: Fetch): Fetch => {
14	  if (customFetch) {
15	    return (...args: Parameters<Fetch>) => customFetch(...args)
16	  }
17	  return (...args: Parameters<Fetch>) => fetch(...args)
18	}

20	export const resolveHeadersConstructor = () => {
21	  return Headers
22	}
23	
24	/**
25	 * New-format Supabase API keys (`sb_publishable_…` / `sb_secret_…`) are not JWTs and
26	 * must never be sent as a Bearer token — they belong only in the `apikey` header.
27	 * All other keys (legacy JWT keys, `sb_temp_…` temporary keys, unrecognized `sb_`
28	 * subtypes) keep the Bearer fallback.
29	 */
30	const isNewApiKey = (key: string): boolean =>
31	  key.startsWith('sb_publishable_') || key.startsWith('sb_secret_')
32	
33	const TEMP_KEY_PREFIX = 'sb_temp_'
34	
35	const warnedKeySubtypes = new Set<string>()
36	
37	/**
38	 * Warn (once per subtype) when an `sb_` key isn't a subtype this SDK version recognizes.
39	 * Never throws — the server, not the SDK, decides key validity. The key value is never
40	 * included in the message.
41	 */
42	export const checkApiKeyFormat = (key: string): void => {
43	  if (!key.startsWith('sb_') || isNewApiKey(key) || key.startsWith(TEMP_KEY_PREFIX)) {
44	    return
45	  }
46	  const subtype = key.match(/^sb_[a-zA-Z0-9]+_/)?.[0] ?? 'unknown'
47	  if (warnedKeySubtypes.has(subtype)) {
48	    return
49	  }
50	  warnedKeySubtypes.add(subtype)
51	  console.warn(
52	    '@supabase/supabase-js: Unrecognized Supabase API key format. The client will proceed ' +
53	      'and send this key as-is; if you see authentication errors you may need to upgrade ' +
54	      '@supabase/supabase-js to a version that recognizes this key type.'
55	  )
56	}
57	
58	export const fetchWithAuth = (
59	  supabaseKey: string,
60	  supabaseUrl: string,
61	  getAccessToken: () => Promise<string | null>,
62	  customFetch?: Fetch,
63	  tracePropagationOptions?: TracePropagationOptions,
64	  options?: { omitApiKeyAsBearer?: boolean }
65	): Fetch => {
66	  const fetch = resolveFetch(customFetch)
67	  const HeadersConstructor = resolveHeadersConstructor()
68	
69	  // Pre-compute trace propagation state once. When disabled, the per-request
70	  // path skips all tracing work with a single truthy check.
71	  const traceEnabled = tracePropagationOptions?.enabled === true
72	  const respectSampling = tracePropagationOptions?.respectSamplingDecision !== false
73	  const traceTargets: TracePropagationTarget[] | null = traceEnabled

75	    : null

78	  // session token. Disabled for Edge Functions with a new-format key (see `isNewApiKey`).
79	  // Static per instance, so it is computed once here rather than on every request.
80	  const allowKeyAsBearer = !(options?.omitApiKeyAsBearer && isNewApiKey(supabaseKey))
81	
82	  return async (input, init) => {
83	    const realToken = await getAccessToken()
84	    let headers = new HeadersConstructor(init?.headers)

86	    if (!headers.has('apikey')) {

88	    }

91	      const bearer = realToken ?? (allowKeyAsBearer ? supabaseKey : null)
92	      if (bearer) {
93	        headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${bearer}`)
94	      }
95	    }
96	
97	    if (traceTargets) {
98	      const traceHeaders = getTraceHeaders(input, traceTargets, respectSampling)
99	
100	      if (traceHeaders) {
101	        if (traceHeaders.traceparent && !headers.has('traceparent')) {
102	          headers.set('traceparent', traceHeaders.traceparent)
103	        }
104	        if (traceHeaders.tracestate && !headers.has('tracestate')) {
105	          headers.set('tracestate', traceHeaders.tracestate)
106	        }
107	        if (traceHeaders.baggage && !headers.has('baggage')) {
108	          headers.set('baggage', traceHeaders.baggage)
109	        }
110	      }
111	    }

113	    return fetch(input, { ...init, headers })
114	  }

117	let warnedMissingTracingRuntime = false
118	let warnedNonW3CPropagator = false

124	 */
125	export function _resetTracingRuntimeWarning(): void {
126	  warnedMissingTracingRuntime = false
127	}

131	 *
132	 * @internal
133	 */
134	export function _resetNonW3CPropagatorWarning(): void {

136	}

138	function getTraceHeaders(
139	  input: RequestInfo | URL,
140	  targets: TracePropagationTarget[],
141	  respectSampling: boolean
142	): TraceContext | null {
143	  // Read the registry before the target check so the warning fires on the
144	  // first request with tracing enabled, not only on Supabase-target ones.
145	  // Reading per request (one globalThis property access) deliberately
146	  // supports late registration: with ESM evaluation order, `createClient`
147	  // can run in a module evaluated before the application entry point's
148	  // `import '@supabase/supabase-js/tracing'`.
149	  const extractTraceContext = getTraceContextExtractor()
150	
151	  if (!extractTraceContext) {
152	    if (!warnedMissingTracingRuntime) {
153	      warnedMissingTracingRuntime = true
154	      console.warn(
155	        '@supabase/supabase-js: tracePropagation is enabled but the tracing runtime is not loaded, ' +
156	          "so trace headers will not be attached. Add `import '@supabase/supabase-js/tracing'` at " +
157	          'your application entry point (requires the OpenTelemetry API package to be installed). ' +
158	          'The CDN/UMD build does not support trace propagation.'
159	      )
160	    }
161	    return null
162	  }
163	
164	  const targetUrl: string | URL =
165	    typeof input === 'string' ? input : input instanceof URL ? input : input.url
166	
167	  if (!shouldPropagateToTarget(targetUrl, targets)) {
168	    return null
169	  }
170	
171	  const traceContext = extractTraceContext()
172	
173	  if (!traceContext || !traceContext.traceparent) {
174	    // An active propagator that writes vendor headers but no W3C
175	    // `traceparent` (e.g. Sentry without `propagateTraceparent: true`) is
176	    // otherwise indistinguishable from "no active trace" — warn once so the
177	    // user learns why no trace headers are attached. An empty carrier means
178	    // no active trace: normal, stay silent.
179	    if (traceContext?.carrierKeys?.length && !warnedNonW3CPropagator) {
180	      warnedNonW3CPropagator = true
181	      const sentryHint = traceContext.carrierKeys.includes('sentry-trace')
182	        ? ' Sentry detected: set `propagateTraceparent: true` in Sentry.init() to emit it.'
183	        : ' Configure your tracing SDK to emit W3C trace context on outgoing requests.'
184	      console.warn(
185	        '@supabase/supabase-js: tracePropagation is enabled and a tracing SDK is active, but its ' +
186	          `propagator wrote [${traceContext.carrierKeys.join(', ')}] and no W3C traceparent header, ` +
187	          'so trace headers will not be attached.' +
188	          sentryHint
189	      )
190	    }
191	    return null
192	  }
193	
194	  if (respectSampling) {
195	    const parsed = parseTraceParent(traceContext.traceparent)
196	    if (parsed && !parsed.isSampled) {
197	      // Unsampled traces still carry `traceparent` so Supabase logs get a
198	      // trace_id to correlate on; the flag stays `00`, so downstream tracing
199	      // never records it as sampled. `tracestate` and `baggage` (the
200	      // vendor/application data channels) are withheld on these requests.
201	      return { traceparent: traceContext.traceparent }
202	    }
203	  }
204	
205	  return traceContext

While you can implement a custom auth solution, for increased security and simplicity, we recommend using an authentication library. These offer built-in solutions for authentication, session management, and authorization, as well as additional features such as social logins, multi-factor authentication, and role-based access control. 1011:## Authorization

1015:There are two main types of authorization checks:
1022:- Creating a [Data Access Layer](#creating-a-data-access-layer-dal) to centralize your authorization logic
1133:We recommend creating a DAL to centralize your data requests and authorization logic.

1181:> **Good to know**: React's [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) deduplicates within a React render pass. Server Actions and Route Handlers are not part of a render pass, so the wrapper does nothing and every call runs the function.

1309:By centralizing your data requests and authorization logic in a DAL and using DTOs, you can ensure that all data requests are secure and consistent, making it easier to maintain, audit, and debug as your application scales.
1364:For example, consider a shared layout that fetches the user data and displays the user image in a nav. Instead of doing the auth check in the layout, you should fetch the user data (`getUser()`) in the layout and do the auth check in your [DAL](#creating-a-data-access-layer-dal).
1366:This guarantees that wherever `getUser()` is called within your application, the auth check is performed, and prevents developers from forgetting to check that the user is authorized to access the data.

For that pattern, see [Using React's `use` within a Context Provider](/docs/app/guides/single-page-applications#using-reacts-use-within-a-context-provider), and use React's [`taintUniqueValue`](https://react.dev/reference/react/experimental_taintUniqueValue) API to keep sensitive session fields from reaching the client.

1507:### Route Handlers
1509:Treat [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) with the same security considerations as public-facing API endpoints, and verify if the user is allowed to access the Route Handler.
1559:The example above demonstrates a Route Handler with a two-tier security check. It first checks for an active session, and then verifies if the logged-in user is an 'admin'.
1628:This example demonstrates an API Route with a two-tier security check for authentication and authorization. It first checks for an active session, and then verifies if the logged-in user is an 'admin'. This approach ensures secure access, limited to authenticated and authorized users, maintaining robust security for request processing.

content.content:
### (a) Publishable keys (`sb_publishable_...`)

- **`apikey` header vs. Bearer:** The page says to send publishable and secret keys on the header, not as a Bearer token: "Send publishable and secret keys on the `apikey` header, not on `Authorization: Bearer`."
- **JWT status:** The page says these keys are not JWTs. Because of that, a tool that verifies a token as a JWT will reject one.
- **Replacing `anon`:** The page doesn't explicitly say a publishable key is a direct one-to-one swap for the `anon` key in the `apikey` header. It describes `anon` as the "Legacy version of publishable keys," and says Supabase is deprecating `anon` by the end of 2026.
- **Coexistence:** "Creating publishable and secret keys doesn't revoke your legacy keys."

### (b) Secret keys (`sb_secret_...`)

- **`apikey` header for Data API, Storage, and Auth admin:** The page doesn't name these services. Its header rule covers both key types: publishable and secret keys go on the `apikey` header.
- **JWT status:** The page says secret keys are short strings rather than JWTs: "Publishable and secret keys are short strings, not JWTs."
- **Authorization Bearer:** The page doesn't allow it. It says the keys aren't JWTs, so "anything that tries to verify one as a JWT fails." It also notes that the `verify_jwt` platform check accepts them on either header for migration compatibility, but "passing that check doesn't authenticate the caller."

### (c) Browser use of secret keys

- The page says a secret key won't work in a browser: "A secret key doesn't work in a browser."
- The enforcement mechanism is that "Supabase matches on the `User-Agent` header and returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized."
- The page still says secret keys must never go in a browser, "even on `localhost`."
- The browser block isn't a safeguard against leaks: "an attacker can still use the key from other tools," so a leaked key should be deleted right away.

The search didn't turn up a Prisma 7 source that mentions `.env.local` directly, but it did surface the main points.

- **Prisma 7 doesn't auto-load `.env`.** A third-party Prisma 7 migration guide says the CLI no longer loads `.env` files on its own, and it suggests loading them explicitly, such as with `import 'dotenv/config'` in `prisma.config.ts` (Prisma CLI no longer auto-loads `.env` files in v7. Explicitly load env vars (for example `import 'dotenv/config'` in `prisma.config.ts`, or load env in your scripts).). This is not an official Prisma source, so verify it against the release notes.
- **The official v7 config example uses the same import.** Its sample `prisma.config.ts` starts with `import "dotenv/config"` and then calls `defineConfig` with `url: env("DATABASE_URL")` (Example: import "dotenv/config"; import { defineConfig, env } from "prisma/config";).
- **Custom file names need a path option.** The official v7 environment-variables page shows dotenv's `config({ path })` call being used to pick an env file by environment (import { config } from "dotenv"; const envFile = process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" ? ".env.development" : ".env.production"; config({ path: envFile });). The same pattern should work with `.env.local`, but I didn't find a Prisma source that confirms it for `prisma.config.ts`.

Likely fix, based on these sources and standard dotenv behavior: in `prisma.config.ts`, call dotenv's `config({ path: ".env.local" })` before `defineConfig` runs, instead of relying on `import "dotenv/config"`, which reads only `.env` by default. Also check the dotenv documentation on variables that are already set in the environment. Since ESM imports are hoisted, moving the `config()` call into its own imported module may be safer than putting it in the file body. I didn't verify that last point against a source.

- "Any environment variables defined in that `.env` file will automatically be loaded when running a Prisma CLI command."

- "Prisma ORM always reads environment variables from the system's environment."

The page's `dotenv` examples are for application code, where it says "you need to load them manually in your application code (for example, by using dotenv)."

**`.env.local`:** The page doesn't mention it.

- supabase-js 2.118.0 treats sb_publishable_ and sb_secret_ as non-JWT (node_modules/@supabase/supabase-js/src/lib/fetch.ts:24-31). It sets the apikey header (fetch.ts:86-88). With no session, the main fetch falls back to sending the key as Bearer (fetch.ts:80, 90-93). Only functionsFetch omits it (src/SupabaseClient.ts:379-386).
- Supabase docs (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/api-keys) say publishable and secret keys go in the apikey header, "not on Authorization: Bearer". They also say "Publishable and secret keys are short strings, not JWTs", and that a secret key is blocked in browsers by User-Agent (401). The page does not name Storage or Auth admin, so Storage/admin acceptance of sb_ keys: not found. Local PostgREST/Storage acceptance: not verified (dryrun has no sb_ key usage; its stack is down).

DOTENV / PRISMA
- dotenv 18.0.9 installed (node_modules/dotenv/package.json). dist/index.d.ts:40 default path is `.env`. dist/index.d.ts:48 types `path?: string | string[] | URL`. README.md:634-637 shows `config({ path: ['.env.local', '.env'] })`; the first value wins unless override is set.
- dryrun prisma7.config.ts:3 `import "dotenv/config";` loads `.env` only (default per index.d.ts:40), not `.env.local`.
- Prisma v7 env docs (https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/more/development-environment/environment-variables): the CLI auto-loads `.env` ("Any environment variables defined in that `.env` file will automatically be loaded when running a Prisma CLI command"). The page does not mention `.env.local` or dotenv in prisma.config.ts. A third-party search summary said the CLI does not auto-load `.env`. The official page contradicts it, so I used the official page.
- Reasoning, not run: a `config({ path })` call in the file body, before defineConfig reads process.env.DATABASE_URL, would run first.
- `directUrl`: not found in node_modules/prisma/config.d.ts or dist/cli/src/config.d.ts.

NEXT 16 / BEARER
- headers.md:45-59: `headers()` is async; `(await headers()).get('authorization')`.
- route.md:258 shows `request.headers` in route handlers.
- authentication.md:1507-1509: treat Route Handlers as public endpoints and verify the user. A grep for "Bearer" in authentication.md found nothing.
- auth-js src/GoTrueClient.ts:3218-3225: `getUser(jwt)` passes the jwt to `_getUser`. Lines 3247-3254 send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` to `${url}/user`. This is a call to the Auth server, not a local decode.
- BRIEF.md:234 requires accepting the Bearer header as well as the session cookie.
